scope: One deliberately idle Tailscale-down fault on the existing private Linux host, observed through an already authenticated owner Chrome session. No recipient grant, active task, model call, or new release was involved.
limits: This check exercised an idle owner browser session, not a recipient session or an active Kata job submitted through the browser.
Chrome's network error was observed after the fault, but no browser request timing or hard outage deadline was measured.
The old owner session did not survive service restart; a fresh Google OIDC sign-in succeeded. This is fail-closed session behavior, not seamless reconnection.
The close hook could not verify the normal inbound shield after tailnet down and used its daemon-blocking fallback. This observed fallback does not prove a universal deadline or recovery reliability.
The separate fifth root-only active-Kata fault passed its bounded checks; this browser check must not be presented as the same end-to-end active-job test.
Historical failed active-fault attempts and the unexplained fourth-attempt relapse remain open. Broad security assurance and pilot readiness remain unproven.
